items: Good AI saves your team time and money, ties to results you already track, such as guest satisfaction or resolution speed, and gets better as you use it.
Bad AI creates rework, makes tone-deaf or inaccurate decisions, can't explain what it's doing and stays static, so your team stops trusting and using it.
AI that can't see your customer history, sales or inventory is guessing, so choose tools that plug into the systems you already use.
Before you buy, ask whether the tool reduces workload, links to a clear outcome, will be trusted by your team and connects to your stack.
